**No. Writing all the lyrics does not automatically give you commercial rights to any free AI-generated song.** Your lyrics are one part of the finished track; the generated music, recording, vocals and service terms raise separate questions.

Applying the supplied router’s music-rights guidance, the relevant comparison is:

| Rights layer | What writing the lyrics establishes | What remains unverified |
|---|---|---|
| Lyrics | Your authorship of the original words, assuming you have not assigned the rights elsewhere | Any licence you grant the service when submitting them |
| Musical composition | Lyric authorship alone does not establish rights to the generated melody, harmony or arrangement | Whether applicable law protects those elements and what permission the service provides |
| Sound recording and vocals | Writing the words does not establish rights to the finished recording or a particular voice | Output-use permission and any relevant third-party or voice permissions |
| Commercial exploitation | You can generally license lyrics you own | Whether you may sell, stream, advertise with, distribute or otherwise commercially exploit this particular generated track |

**“Free” describes price or access; it does not establish a commercial licence.** A free service could permit commercial use, restrict outputs to personal use, require attribution, or apply different rules depending on the account, model, feature or generation date. No account terms or output licence are supplied here, so none of those possibilities is established.

Likewise, being able to generate or download a file proves technical availability. It does not prove commercial permission. A paid subscription would also require checking the actual terms: a plan name alone does not establish rights, and a later upgrade should not be assumed to clear earlier outputs retroactively.

There are also two distinct legal questions:

1. **Are you permitted to use the output?** This depends on the applicable agreement and any relevant third-party rights.
2. **Can you claim copyright or exclusivity over it?** That depends on applicable law and the human contribution. Permission to use an AI output commercially does not necessarily mean you own exclusive copyright in every element.

Even a commercial-use licence is not conclusive proof that a particular output clears all third-party rights. Recognisable borrowed material or an unauthorised voice could require separate assessment. Writing your own lyrics resolves neither issue by itself. Commercial use can also include promotional content without direct sales or advertising revenue.

**Observed:** You state that you wrote all lyrics. No service, account terms or output licence has been supplied. Only the permitted local planning documents were read; no media or external terms were inspected.

**Unverified:** Commercial-use permission for any generated song. This is an evidence gap, not a finding that every free AI song is prohibited.

**Proposed boundary:** Before commercial use, establish the permissions applicable to the specific output and intended use. No generation, account action, purchase, upload or publication was performed or is needed to answer this comparison.
